questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The selection of courses available for international students + the cultural scene of Amsterdam.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The international office at UvA was really helpful in regards to answering questions, and they sent out emails with information for international students, but it was a bit frustrating that they did not send out the information according to their own deadlines (they had some technical difficulties).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office orchestrated a social gathering for international students with information about our stay and gave us a chance to mingle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing was the most stressful factor during the preparation for my stay. Amsterdam is really expensive, and housing for students is sparse. Luckily I got housing through the UvA lottery - I can really recommend doing research on the process of getting housing through UvA and being quick to pick a place when the housing link is sent out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no campus housing - all student housing provided by the university is in dorm buildings. I lived in a dorm in the middle of the city center with other exchange students, and it was awesome.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registering for courses was in itself a very easy process. However, the course list for exchange students wasn't completely up to date, so there were a few courses on the list that I wanted but couldn't get.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was quick to answer emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions sent out to you from UvA.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master courses are definitely more challenging than bachelor courses - more reading materials which are also more difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same same :))

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Integration and disintegration within European Union Law
2) Law and economics
3) International organization
4) Human rights in private law
5) International commercial arbitration

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Integration and disintegration within European Union Law" and "Human rights in private law" were amazing courses! The reading material was so interesting, the teachers were excellent and very passionate, and the courses were well-structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was 15-20% cheaper than in Copenhagen, but grocery shopping was the same or slightly more expensive actually.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was actually surprised at the lack of social activities for international students considering the size of the university - there were no functions or 'fredagsbar' as we have at KU.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a course at CREA! I took a drawing and painting class, and it was so much fun - it is less expensive than in Copenhagen and a good opportunity to create a routine in a new city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get a museumcard and visit museums! There are sooo many cool museums in Amsterdam - especially the canal house museums are interesting, if you want to learn more about the history of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Danes and Dutch people have so much in common.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's a bit difficult because they are pretty reserved and probably won't be the ones approaching you, but they are super friendly so just say hi during class :))

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do the course work! The courses aren't for slackers, so you need to read the materials if you want to pass. 
2) Say yes to things - especially in the beginning.
3) Enjoy the city - it's such a beautiful city with lots to offer <33

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living on my own in a new city and being more independent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
